subject: BYO key handoff acceptance checks and network ops preflight

Date: Sat, 3 May 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: BYO key handoff — acceptance checks and network ops preflight

Hi Rishi / Monica —

Thanks again for the runthrough yesterday. Acme's infra team wants to confirm the exact acceptance checks Redwood will run during the BYO (bring-your-own-key) handoff window. Our priority is to validate that:

- The HSM key import completes with the expected key attributes (algorithm, key usage, labels)
- Operator separation is preserved (no operator service account has plaintext access)
- Network egress rules prevent unauthorized callbacks during attestation phases
- Rotation paths and emergency zeroize are triggerable from our side after cutover

Can you share the acceptance checklist you intend to run (ideally with the specific network / firewall rules ephemeral ports and expected CIDR ranges)? We need that to schedule our maintenance window with change control.

Also, please confirm whether any part of the import relies on vendor-managed outbound endpoints (we prefer non-internet egress).

Attached: preliminary inventory of secrets and the change control template from our side.

Regards,
Alex Gomez
Lead Cloud Ops — Acme Payments

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: BYO key handoff — acceptance checks and network ops preflight

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is the acceptance checklist we'll execute from Redwood's side during the handoff; I've included the network expectations and the operator/role assertions. I've attached an editable checklist and a rotation matrix as well.

Summary (high level):
1) Validate key metadata post-import (RSA-2048 / EC P-256 flags as requested)
2) Validate policy bindings: customer-admin (Acme) vs operator (Redwood ops) separation — operator roles are limited to attestation and HSM appliance health, no unwrap/sign permissions for keys labeled BYO_APP_KEYS
3) Offline attestation: vendor-supplied attestation blob will be verified locally; no outbound to vendor attestation endpoints required
4) Network constraints:
   - Incoming control plane: allow management from Redwood control plane IPs (10.142.8.0/29) via mutual TLS to port 8443
   - HSM provisioning traffic: must be allowed from Acme on-prem orchestration host (192.168.42.10) to the HSM over the private cross-connect; no public internet egress needed
   - Backup/escrow handshake: customer will place wrapped key shares in S3-compatible escrow endpoint residing in Acme VPC (no public bucket)
5) Rotation & emergency: validate that rotation job can be initiated by Acme service account (acme-kms-rotation@acme-ops.com) and that operator zeroize requires multi-party operator approval

Please review the attached 'redline_byo_handoff_checklist.pdf' and 'rotation_matrix_v1.xlsx' — I've highlighted the items that will block cutover if not green.

Next steps: propose two candidate windows (we recommend a 3-hour window) and designate an Acme on-call to run acceptance sign-off.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Rishi — this is great and granular, thank you. A couple of clarifications from our side after reviewing the PDF:

- The clause about "Redwood control plane IPs (10.142.8.0/29)" — our network team asked for fully qualified hostnames or the single elastic IPs so we can pin in the firewall. Can Redwood provide the outbound EIP(s) used for the handoff?
- For the escrow flow: we will host the S3-compatible endpoint in a restricted subnet. Do you require a specific S3 API version or any special metadata on the wrapped shares?
- Emergency zeroize: to confirm, the zeroize operation requires two Redwood operator approvals plus one Acme admin? If so, please add that to the checklist explicitly.

We can do the window on Tuesday May 6 between 02:00–05:00 UTC. I'll put ops on-call.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — quick answers from networking/security ops:

- We will provide two dedicated EIPs for the transient control-plane connections; final IPs will be circulated 48 hours before the window. If you need hostnames instead, we can bind them to the EIPs and share DNS entries.
- Wrapped shares: Redwood expects AES-KW wrapped shares using RFC 3394; metadata fields we add are: origin=redwood-handoff, version=1, key-id (UUID). If your escrow endpoint has object metadata enforcement we can add any additional tags you require.
- Zeroize flow: confirmed — zeroize requires two Redwood operator approvals; Acme can trigger a zeroize request, but the action is gated by Redwood operator approvals. We'll add a manual override clause for disaster recovery which requires an additional signed DocuSign approval from Acme's security director.

Ben — can you attach the RBAC snippet and the ephemeral firewall rules to this thread? I highlighted them in the checklist.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Alex / team — attaching the RBAC snippet and the ephemeral firewall ACL example. A couple of operational notes:

- RBAC: The 'redwood-ops-handoff' role has only two permissions: hsm:attest and hsm:healthcheck. All key lifecycle operations (import, wrap/unwrap, rotate, zeroize) are controlled by the 'acme-kms-admin' role. We enforce this using policy bindings in the HSM operator and an IAM bridge in the cross-connect.
- Firewall ACL: During the handoff window, allow inbound from 54.221.12.9 and 54.221.12.10 to port 8443 (mTLS) and allow management from 192.168.42.10 on the private link for provisioning. All other egress is blocked.
- Audit: We will stream attestation and import events to an SQS queue in Acme's account for the 30-day retention period you requested; audit records will include operator principal and a signed attestation blob.

I'm good with Tuesday May 6 02:00–05:00 UTC.

-ben
Ben Carter
